description:
PearCal is a peer-to-peer calendar app that syncs directly between devices — no server, no cloud, no accounts required.

Your calendar data never leaves your group. It lives only on the devices of the people you choose to share with, powered by Hypercore Protocol.

FEATURES

Peer Groups

Create a group and invite others via a share link or QR code. Each group has its own color and avatar. Members see only the events shared with them.

Events & Reminders

Create one-time or recurring events. Set a reminder time per event. Selectively share events with specific group members — not everyone in a group has to see every event.

Holidays
Optional US, Canada, and UK public holiday calendars. Toggle per country from your profile. Holiday events are read-only and stored locally only.

Privacy First

No account creation. No email address. No tracking. No ads. Your data stays on your devices.

Open Source
PearCal is free and open source. Source code is available on GitHub.

PERMISSIONS

Camera — used to set your profile photo and scan QR invite codes.
Photo Library — used to set your profile photo.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

New Features
  - Open calendar files straight into PearCal. Tap a calendar file (.ics) in your email, Files or another app, or share it to PearCal, and the import screen opens on its own.
  - Desktop: you can now hand a group over to another member, or claim a group whose owner has been inactive for more than 30 days.
  - Desktop: "Reset app data" is now in Settings. Clear your calendar and groups and stay the same person, or start over as a new user.

Improvements
  - Repeating events now carry over when you import a calendar file. Birthdays and other yearly, monthly, weekly or daily events from Google, Apple or Yandex keep repeating instead of showing up only once.
  - Exporting keeps repeating events as a single repeating entry, so "repeat forever" events keep all their future dates and other calendar apps see one series instead of hundreds of copies.
  - Importing a file you already imported no longer creates duplicates of repeating events.
  - If a calendar file has no events PearCal can read, you now get a short message instead of nothing happening.
